text:
The last session was too long so a new one is started. We were discussing "direct rule injection" in our AGI system. We plan to build an NL→logic→DLN mapper and you outlined some steps and issues. You wrote: "predicates and modifiers don’t neatly align to a fixed embedding/key space—sense disambiguation, OOVs, and consistent mapping of paraphrases/synonyms all require either a robust semantic linker or a learned adapter, otherwise rules fragment and fail to compose."
That was insightful. It seems that the mapper requires highly intelligent rules for itself. Can such rules be learned? This is a meta-learning problem and may give us more useful ideas.

If theres is a bias towards shorter and more general rules, those rules can become established in the DLN (ie, with high confidence) and become canonical without supervision or explicit bias. Injection requires a special step of transferring a logical form to DLN, which is not normally there. I want to 1) identify the loss/reward pathway that enables learning the additional rules for injection, and 2) seed with some key rules along this path to accelerate learning.  That seems to be very cost-effective, right?

I mean, if we have the special mechanism that transfers a logical form to DLN, can the rest be achieved using symbolic rules within the symbolic engine and nothing else?  And this idea may extend to similar mechanisms of meta-learning?

I see. Bayesian / bandit-style updates are sufficient because we're not modifying the rules themselves. In the meta-learning idea, we seem to lack a mechanism to invent rules although this could follow ILP traditional practices.  Then we seem to have a general meta-learning mechanism?

So the addition of a rule to DLN is the key step towards meta-reasoning. The same route is also achievable by adding rules to the symbolic-engine side. In categorical logic this is the -^A ⊢ (-×A) adjuction and also called "Cartesian closure". Perhaps it is the most general form of meta-reasoning as far as logic is concerned?
SO we need to "score" the symbolic rule-base, either "Bayesian" or bandit-style as you suggested. Would the Bayesian approach be too costly to scale?
Good. Can you share the gist as an .md file about the scheme of meta-reasoning? We would focus on the rules injection part for now, but do mention there are other aspects.
Please resume our developments, taking our discussions into account.  What should be our next steps?
Yes, please proceed to implement a simple form of rule-injection.
you can use the venv environment!

Prior to this, we were trying to make training "labels", and I suggested to directly transfer hand-crafted rules from the symbolic side to DLN.  Are we closer to that target now?  Can this make the label generation process faster?  So that we can tackle large-scale datasets....
Yes, please implement the above (simplifying if it gets too complicated) and prepare to test it on TinyStories.
